query: The Good Boat {The boathouse has six boats that leak and one, the blue one, that doesn't. The boatman keeps it for himself and sits on it to make the point.|The blue boat, the boatman, the folded arms. You've started to think of them as one animal.|The boatman sees you coming and settles more firmly onto the blue boat. "No," he says, before you've asked.} Pay his price for an hour {He takes your crowns, counts them twice and lets you have the blue boat for exactly an hour. It's the stillest hour you've spent all term.|An hour on the lake in a boat that doesn't sink. You row out to the middle and lie back and watch the towers upside down.|You pay. He watches you the whole hour, from the jetty, as if you'd borrowed his dog.} Take the green one, bailing {You take the green boat and a bailer. You row half the time and bail the other half. It's still the lake, and still lovely.|The green boat, which takes on water like a sponge. You come back with wet boots and a better opinion of yourself.|You bail all the way out and all the way back. The boatman says you've got a rower's arms now, and charges you nothing for the joke.} Charm him off the blue boat {You turn on a little more charm than you have, and he finds himself telling you about his late wife, and then lending you the blue boat, and then wondering why.|A smile with Glamour in it. The boatman gets up, holds the boat steady for you, and calls you "young sir or madam" like a courtier.|He remembers liking you and not quite why. You get the blue boat for the rest of the day and a cup of his terrible tea after.}
